battle.name: 京襄之戰
battle.brief: 嘉熙二年（1238）春，蒙古大汗國再舉南侵，兵鋒直指襄陽與安慶兩處要衝。宋以孟珙坐鎮荊襄、杜杲固守安慶，沿江築城列砲，遣舟師巡江，以猛火油與霹靂炮焚燬敵舟，與元軍在襄漢、江淮之間拉鋸半年。襄陽未克，安慶圍城數月亦不能下。希臘火那類配銅管噴射的燃燒劑，正是雙方在水陸爭鋒的技術焦點。

kit.name: 希臘火
kit.history: 配在銅管裡的燃燒劑。配方是帝國的機密，配方和船一起沉了。

countries: 交戰一方是蒙古大汗國的帝國軍。一二三五年以來，大汗窩闊台把滅金之師分作東、中、西三道部署，一二三八年再度集兵南向：西道入蜀，中道趨荊襄與兩淮，東道沿淮東下，各路兵由諸王與萬戶分領。編制仍承十戶、百戶、千戶、萬戶的老法，蒙古騎兵是突擊骨幹；漢地降附軍戶與漢人將領所部則擔負攻城、渡江、轉糧之役，配屬工匠、攻具手與探馬。指揮上以大汗居中樞，諸王幕府與新置行省分領各路，前鋒游騎輕進，後隊屯駐待命；糧道自河南、蔡州沿汴、泗、淮諸水而下，就地徵用漢地州縣的粟麥、柴薪與船戶。另一方是南宋朝廷：行在臨安以樞密院掌軍政，兵部與三省分掌調度，沿邊設兩淮、淮西、湖北、四川等路制置司。荊襄一線由孟珙以湖北制置使之節制江防，淮西安慶由知府杜杲專主城守，兩淮由制置使趙葵總理軍務，川蜀由制置司銜接管蜀邊。守軍主力為禁軍與地方鎮兵，沿江諸郡則徵發民兵築城、置砲、輸船，並以御前諸軍與邊軍互相策應。
countriesEn: One side was the imperial army of the Mongol Great Khanate. Since 1235 the Great Khan Ogedei had split his anti-Jin army into an eastern, a central and a western route, and in 1238 he once more massed troops southward: the western route into Shu, the central route toward Jingxiang and the Two Huai, the eastern route down the Huai valley, each column led by its own princes and wanmen. The organisation still followed the old ten-, hundred-, thousand- and ten-thousand-house system, with Mongol cavalry as the striking arm; surrendered Han households and the troops of Han commanders took on the labour of siege, river crossing and supply, supported by craftsmen, masters of siege engines and mounted scouts. Command ran from the Great Khan in the centre, with the princes' staffs and the newly created provincial administrations holding separate routes, light mounted vanguards pressing forward while rear formations waited in place; the supply line came down the Bian, Si and Huai waterways from Henan and Caizhou, drawing grain, firewood and boat crews from the Han prefectures along the way. The other side was the Southern Song court: at Lin'an the Privy Council handled military affairs while the Ministry of War and the Three Departments shared out direction, and along the frontier stood the Military Commissions of the Two Huai, of Huaxi, of Huguang and of Sichuan. The Jingxiang line was under Meng Gong, who as Huguang Military Commissioner directed the river defence; Anqing was in the hands of the prefect Du Gao, who personally directed the defence of the city; the Two Huai was overseen by the Commissioner Zhao Kui; and Sichuan was administered by its own Military Commission. The garrison was formed mainly of imperial guard and regional troops, while the river prefectures levied local militia to build walls, set up crossbow artillery and supply boats, with the palace guards and the frontier armies cross-supporting one another.
people: 蒙古方面，一二三八年南下的兵權仍在窩闊台大汗手中，他於 一二三五年遣闊出、速不台等王將分道入宋，闊出早於 一二三六年病斃於南方軍中，速不台與眾萬戶再統東路兵於 一二三八年沿淮河北下；漢地將領中，張柔以滁州總管之任在淮西一帶游騎掠地。南宋方面，孟珙自 一二三四年起任湖北制置使，總荊襄江防，是這條戰線的樞紐；一二三八年元軍逼近時，他一面遣將拒守襄陽、樊城，一面遣舟師巡江，以火攻焚燬元軍舟糧，又以夜襲焚其營寨積聚，試圖把蒙軍拖在水路與糧道上。杜杲以安慶知府主持城防，築城置砲、募敢死之士，把霹靂炮與弩砲架上城頭，是守城最見功的一環。兩淮方面由趙葵總制，紅襖軍首領李全則在滁、濠、盱眙一帶據地自守，與官軍分進合擊。四川方向抵擋元軍的宋軍將領，與淮南各郡守令，都是這場戰役裡不可忽略的支點。至於《宋史》《元史》對 一二三八年雙方將領姓名與行軍序列的記載頗為零散，許多細節至今難以確證，署名與戰功只能取其大略。
peopleEn: On the Mongol side the authority over the 1238 campaign still rested with the Great Khan Ogedei, who had dispatched princes such as Kocho and Subutai into Song territory in separate columns in 1235; Kocho had died of illness in the southern armies as early as 1236, and Subutai together with the myriad wanmen led the eastern army down the Huai in 1238. Among the Han commanders, Zhang Rou, holding the post of commissioner at Chuzhou, rode raiding parties through the Huai west. On the Song side, Meng Gong, Huguang Military Commissioner from 1234, was the pivot of the whole line: when the Mongol pressure closed in, he sent officers to hold Xiangyang and Fancheng, sent river squadrons to patrol the water, burned the Mongol boats and grain with fire, and struck by night to set fire to the enemy's camps and stores, in the hope of pinning the Mongols to the water and to the supply road. Du Gao, prefect of Anqing, directed the defence of the city, building walls, mounting crossbow artillery, recruiting men for desperate service and setting thunder-crash bombs and heavy crossbows on the battlements, and was the most conspicuous part of that defence. Zhao Kui commanded the Two Huai, while Li Quan, chief of the Red Jacket forces, held ground around Chuzhou, Haozhou and Xuyi in his own way, cooperating with the regular troops. The Song commanders facing the Mongols in the Sichuan direction, and the prefects of the Huai-north prefectures who answered the same appeal from their own posts, are further pivots of this campaign. It should be said that the Songshi and the Yuanshi preserve only scattered names and marching orders for 1238, and many of the details remain unproven, so that the names and the credit of deeds can be given only in broad outline.
kits: 這張卡上的兵器是希臘火——拜占庭帝國在七世紀後期成形的燃燒劑，以銅管與泵把配好的燃料噴向水面或船板，配方是帝國的最高機密，承載配方的船隻沉入海底之後，異族再也造不出同樣的火焰。就本場戰役而言，與它同一技術譜系的陸戰裝備，是宋軍在安慶城頭架設的霹靂炮與猛火油：前者以鐵丸盛油藥、發之聲如雷霆並縱火，後者以竹筒、陶罐盛石油，擲向敵舟或淋灑攻城器械之下；水戰中宋軍舟師同樣以火攻焚燒元軍舟楫，可說是希臘火在遠東的對應物。元軍方面以騎兵迂迴、輕弓速射為主，攻城靠雲梯、撞竿、穴地與石砲一類攻具，並大量徵用漢地工匠改造器械，渡江則用皮囊、革筏與結浮橋諸法。兩軍都配備大量弓弩：宋軍有神臂弓、蹶張弩與弩砲，蒙古弓手則以強弓配撒放箭與穿甲箭，攻城時配合飛石與火燒攻城塔。運輸方面，元軍倚河運糧、以牛車與馬匹轉輸器械，宋軍則靠漕船與改裝漁船運糧輸兵，並在沿江諸堡寨屯儲糧秣柴薪，以維持長達數月的圍城與拒守。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is Greek fire: an incendiary mixture which the Byzantine Empire had brought to maturity in the later seventh century, pumped through copper pipes and jets toward the water or the planking of ships, its formula the empire's highest secret, and once the vessel carrying the formula went down with the formula aboard, no foreign power could produce the same flame again. In this campaign the land counterpart of that same technological family was the thunder-crash bomb and the fierce fire oil which the Song mounted on the walls of Anqing: the first, iron balls filled with oil and drugs, burst with a thunderous report and set fire as they flew; the second, bamboo tubes and earthen jars of petroleum, were thrown at enemy boats or poured over the siege engines below the walls. The Song river squadrons likewise answered with fire against the Mongol fleet, so that the Anqing weapons and the burning on the river were the distant-Far-Eastern counterparts of Greek fire. The Mongol army, for its part, relied on cavalry manoeuvre and rapid shooting from light bows, and on ladders, battering rams, tunnelling and stone-throwing engines in the assault, drawing on Han craftsmen to rebuild their machines; crossings were made with skin bladders, hide rafts and floating bridges. Both sides carried great quantities of bows: the Song had the divine arm bow, the powerful crossbow and the mounted crossbow piece, while Mongol archers used strong composite bows with loose and armour-piercing arrows, and in the assault worked with stone-throwers and fire applied to siege towers. In the matter of transport, the Mongols moved grain by river and used ox-carts and horses to shift their engines, while the Song carried grain and troops on canal boats and converted fishing boats, and stored grain, firewood and water in the forts along the river so that siege and defence could be sustained for months.
tactics: 蒙古的作法是把兵力拆成彼此策應的數路：一路沿淮北平原掃清州縣，切斷江南的漕運與鹽利；一路直取荊襄外圍的江北諸城，企圖先取江陵、襄陽外圍據點，把襄陽孤立；一路入蜀，把川蜀的注意力釘在山地里，好讓中路的攻城不受牽制。臨江的兵則以舟師配合騎兵：騎兵先以皮囊、木排漂渡，舟師隨之在江面展開，試圖控制水面，使宋軍的援兵無法上下江。攻城採圍三闕一、主力集於一面的辦法，並同步斷糧、斷援、斷水，逼迫守軍在城內消耗；宋軍的應對則是以江為險：自鄂州至襄陽沿江修築堡寨、關隘與砲壘，節節設防，舟師不斷巡江，遇元軍舟隊即以火攻與弩砲襲擊；城頭以弩砲封鎖江面航道，射擊覆舟，攻城戰中則集中火力射擊雲梯與攻具，密集的弩矢在城頭形成封鎖，使元軍的攀登屢試屢敗。孟珙更以夜襲為主，派小股精兵乘夜焚燬元營積聚與舟糧，使蒙軍不敢在江岸久屯；杜杲在安慶則採以守待攻、築砲以備的辦法，招募敢死、改造舊砲，專以射擊攻具與焚燒攻城塔為務，並在城郊修築第二道城垣以縱深防守。
tacticsEn: The Mongols split their force into several mutually supporting columns: one swept the prefectures of the northern Huai plain, cutting the canal traffic and the salt revenues of the south; another struck at the towns on the northern bank outside Jingxiang, hoping to seize the outer posts around Jiangling and Xiangyang first so that Xiangyang itself would be isolated; a third went into Sichuan, pinning the Song's attention in the mountains so that the central column could siege without being harried. Along the river the force combined horsemen with the flotilla: cavalry crossed first on hide bladders and timber rafts, the boats then deployed on the water in an attempt to control the surface so that Song reinforcements could not move up or down the river. Besieges were conducted by leaving one side of the city open and concentrating the main effort on a single face, while at the same time cutting grain, cutting relief and cutting water to wear the garrison down inside its walls. The Song answered by making the river their fortress: from Ezhou to Xiangyang they raised forts, passes and artillery positions along the bank and defended stage by stage, while squadrons patrolled the water continuously and met Mongol flotillas with fire and crossbow artillery. On the walls, mounted crossbow pieces sealed the river channels, dropping fire on boats, and in the assault the defenders concentrated their shooting on the ladders and engines, so that the massed crossbow bolts from the wall formed a curtain that repeatedly spoiled the Mongol climbing. Meng Gong made night attacks his chief arm, sending small bodies of picked men to burn the enemy's stores and boats by night so that the Mongols would not dare to stand long on the bank. At Anqing Du Gao chose to wait behind walls, raising artillery and recruiting volunteers, his business being the shooting of siege engines and the burning of towers, and he built a second line of works outside the city to give the defence depth.
data: 可用的數字大致如下：一二三八年元軍動用的兵馬，舊籍常寫數十萬，但以當時的徵發與糧秣條件衡量，兩路同時南下的兵數各以數萬計較為可信。杜杲在安慶城頭架設的弩砲，記載為數十具；孟珙在荊襄沿江所設的堡寨與砲壘分佈在數百里江防線上，巡江舟師的規模以數百艘計。圍攻安慶自嘉熙二年冬延續至翌年春天，歷數月而不能下。孟珙焚燬元軍舟糧一事，史料只說舟楫為之一空，沒有留下確數，但可見蒙軍水上運輸線受創之深。就距離而言，自襄陽順漢水、長江而下至安慶，約一千二百里水路；由襄陽至臨安，則須越過整條江淮防線。這一戰線上雙方拉鋒的時間，自 一二三八年春開春出兵，到 一二三八年十二月大汗病逝於蔡州，前後約九個月。蒙古在 一二三八年一度攻取池州、滁州、濠州等江淮據點，卻未能打通南北；荊襄核心則全線未失。
dataEn: The figures that can be used are roughly these: the old records often put the Mongol army of 1238 at several hundred thousand, but measured against the requisitions and the grain supply actually available, a few tens of thousands for each of the two columns operating at once is the more credible figure. The crossbow artillery Du Gao mounted on the walls of Anqing is recorded as numbering several dozen pieces; Meng Gong's forts and artillery positions along the Jingxiang river were strung out over several hundred li of river defence, and the patrolling river squadrons numbered in the hundreds of boats. The siege of Anqing ran from the winter of the second year of Jiaxi into the following spring, lasting several months without falling. On the burning of the Mongol boats and grain by Meng Gong the sources say only that the river was left empty of hulls, giving no exact count, but the depth of the damage done to the Mongol water-borne supply line is plain. In distance, some twelve hundred li of water run from Xiangyang down the Hanshui and the Yangtze to Anqing, and from Xiangyang to Lin'an the whole Huai river defence line lay in between. The contest on this front lasted about nine months, from the spring start of the campaign in 1238 to the Great Khan's death at Caizhou in December 1238. The Mongols in 1238 did take Chizhou, Chuzhou and Haozhou at points along the Huai, but they never linked north and south; the heart of Jingxiang was never lost.
cause: 直接起因是蒙古在 一二三五年確立滅宋方略後，於 一二三八年再度集兵南侵。一二三六年春，闊出所率中路軍攻入荊襄，襄陽一度失守，闊出隨即病斃於南方軍中，蒙古第一次南下遂止於江漢之間。此後兩年，元廷整軍、造器械、徵糧，漢地州縣被納入軍需體系，騎兵與攻城大隊同時擴充，一二三八年春重新出兵時，攻勢比上一次更重：不再只是抄掠州縣，而是直指江防的核心城邑。同時，南宋朝廷在主和與死守之間搖擺，年貢與和議的往返使邊郡得不到一致的指令；四川方向的牽制、荊襄方向的失守與兩淮的僵持，也讓宋廷屢次考慮以捨荊保淮的取捨換取喘息。這一戰役的真正戰略動機因此十分清楚：元軍要在荊襄打通水路，讓上游的漢中、蜀中與中下游的江淮、江南連成一條線，好使江南的漕運、鹽利與臨安的糧道盡落在蒙古的火力之下；宋軍則要死守這條線上的襄陽與安慶，因為一旦失去兩處，江防就沒有第二道門。
causeEn: The immediate cause was the Mongol decision of 1235 to destroy the Song and the renewed massing of troops in 1238. In the spring of 1236 the central column under Kocho had driven into Jingxiang and Xiangyang had fallen for a time, and Kocho died of illness in the southern armies soon after, so that the first Mongol advance stopped somewhere between the Han and the Yangtze. Over the next two years the Mongol court drilled the army, built engines, levied grain, brought the Han prefectures into the supply system and enlarged both the cavalry and the great siege columns; when the army went out again in the spring of 1238 the offensive was heavier than before, no longer a raid through the prefectures but a drive at the core cities of the river defence. Meanwhile the Southern Song court wavered between seeking peace and holding the line, and the shuttling of envoys over tribute and terms left the frontier prefectures without consistent instructions; the pull of the Sichuan front, the loss of Jingxiang and the stalemate in the Two Huai led the court repeatedly to consider trading away Jingxiang in order to save the Huai. The strategic motive of the campaign is therefore plain: the Mongols meant to open a water route through Jingxiang so that Hanzhong and Shu in the upper reaches would be joined to the Huai and the south below, placing the canal traffic, the salt revenues and the grain road of Lin'an within Mongol reach; the Song meant to hold Xiangyang and Anqing, because once those two were lost the river defence would have no second door.
impact: 其一，荊襄江防自此成為南宋抵禦蒙古的主軸。孟珙總結出的江防三策——築城修壘、依江為險、措置宿將與流民——把宋軍的部署從野戰轉向城防與水寨，釣魚城一類山城防禦體系亦在此後數年由余玠在四川推開。其二，燃燒類兵器在實戰中留下的記載越來越具體：安慶城頭的霹靂炮，是這類武器第一次以可考的規模出現在宋軍的城防裝備裡，與希臘火同屬以化學燃燒劑配合銅管、鐵丸、投擲或噴射的技術譜系，也顯示十三世紀的東亞已把這類武器用於守城與水戰。其三，一二三八年十二月窩闊台大汗病逝於蔡州，蒙古的攻勢為之停頓，汗位繼承的混亂又牽動了前線，兩岸因此換來一段相對安寧的時間，宋廷得以重整沿江諸州。其四，襄陽在此役之後成為雙方必爭之地：一二三六年失而復得、一二三八年鞏固之後，一二六八年再度淪陷、一二七三年襄樊陷落，其實正是這次攻防所埋下的隱憂。蒙古以漢人將領與漢地軍戶編成的混合部隊，亦在這幾年裡成形，成為其後攻宋與滅宋的主幹。
impactEn: First, the Jingxiang river defence became the main axis of the Song's resistance to the Mongols. Meng Gong's three measures for the river defence, building walls and works, taking the river as the barrier, and settling good commanders and displaced people, turned the Song deployment from field battle into fortification and river stockades, and the mountain-city system exemplified by Diaoyu Fortress was opened up in the following years by Yu Jie in Sichuan. Second, the record of incendiary weapons in actual combat grew more and more concrete: the thunder-crash bomb on the walls of Anqing was the first appearance of this class of weapon in the Song's city defences on any verifiable scale, belonging with Greek fire to a single technological family that married a chemical burning agent to copper pipe, iron ball, throwing or jetting, and it showed that in thirteenth-century East Asia such weapons were already in service for the defence of cities and for river warfare. Third, the death of the Great Khan Ogedei at Caizhou in December 1238 halted the Mongol offensive, and the confusion over the succession at the heart of the empire kept the front unsettled; the two banks thus gained a period of relative quiet in which the Song court could reorganise the prefectures along the river. Fourth, Xiangyang became a place both sides had to hold after this campaign: recovered after the loss of 1236 and consolidated in 1238, it was lost again in 1268 and fell in 1273, and that outcome was already implicit in the fighting of 1238. The Mongol practice of mixing Han commanders and Han troops from the conquered prefectures into their armies also took shape in these years and became the backbone of the later war against Song and of its final destruction.
result: 結果是雙方都沒有達到戰略目標。宋軍保住了襄陽與安慶兩處要點，荊襄全線未失；孟珙在江面焚燬元軍舟糧、夜襲焚其營寨積聚，使蒙軍一時不能在水路得手；杜杲在安慶以弩砲與霹靂炮守城數月，元軍終不能拔，攻城器械多被焚燬，暫時退兵。蒙古軍在江淮一線攻取池州、滁州、濠州等城，取得據點卻未能把南北連成一片，江面仍受制於宋軍舟師與弩砲，火攻與反火攻的較量在這一役裡沒有分出勝負。真正改變戰局的是 一二三八年十二月大汗病逝：蒙古軍主力陸續北撤，攻勢中止，宋朝於是守住了這道長江防線的核心段，兩國之間的戰爭再回到拉鋸與消耗的節奏。從長線看，這場戰役的真正結果是雙方都把荊襄與江淮當成了不可放棄的樞紐：蒙古此後二十餘年屢攻此地，宋朝則把有限的兵力與資源長期押在襄陽—安慶—兩淮這條線上，為日後襄樊陷落、偏安終局的結局埋下了伏筆。
resultEn: The result was that neither side reached its strategic aim. The Song held Xiangyang and Anqing, the two pivots, and the whole Jingxiang line was never lost; Meng Gong's fire against the Mongol boats and grain on the river and his night attacks on the enemy's camps and stores kept the Mongols from success on the water for a time; Du Gao held Anqing for months with crossbow artillery and thunder-crash bombs, the besiegers could not take the city and much of their siege material was burned, so they withdrew for the time being. The Mongols took points along the Huai such as Chizhou, Chuzhou and Haozhou, but they never joined north to south, and the water remained under the constraint of the Song squadrons and their crossbow pieces; the duel between fire and counter-fire was not decided in this campaign. What truly changed the situation was the Great Khan's death in December 1238: the main Mongol forces drew back north in succession, the offensive stopped, and the Song thus held the central stretch of the great river line, and the war between the two states returned to a rhythm of attrition and endurance. In the long run the real result of this campaign is that both sides treated Jingxiang and the Huai as pivots that could not be given up: the Mongols attacked here repeatedly for more than twenty years afterwards, and the Song tied down its limited troops and resources on the Xiangyang, Anqing and Two Huai line for the rest of its days, which is where the seed of the later fall of Xiangfan and of the dynasty's end was planted.
